title: Design a cost-optimized architecture
objective: Compare costs and constraints based on usage patterns, performance, availability, data transfer, and the division of responsibilities.

sections.title: Choosing Purchasing and Scaling Strategies Based on Demand Patterns
paragraphs: Cost optimization is not about choosing the option with the lowest unit price. Architects distinguish between always-on workloads, predictable baseline load, variable load, interruptible processing, and response deadlines, then compare the constraints of On-Demand, commitments, Spot, serverless, and auto scaling.

Commitments are suitable for portions of usage expected to remain stable, while Spot is suitable for workloads that can tolerate interruption. For every approach, verify capacity shortages, eviction, retries, scaling time, and service objectives, and confirm that cost reductions are not increasing user impact.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Pricing Models and Sizing

sections.title: Visualize and optimize data movement and storage
paragraphs: Before optimizing data transfer costs, measure what is moving between users, the edge, Regions, AZs, VPCs, on-premises environments, and origins, and how much is moving. Changing network paths affects not only costs but also latency, availability, security inspections, and the paths used during failures.

For storage, compare access frequency, restoration time, minimum storage duration, data volume, durability, and retention obligations. Even when introducing lifecycle transitions or caching, failure to verify deletion protection, restoration tests, and cache freshness can turn cost savings into unrecoverable data or inconsistencies.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Data Transfer and Storage

sections.title: Tie Costs Back to Owners and Design Decisions
paragraphs: The cost of shared infrastructure cannot be optimized based on the total bill alone. Architects design tags or allocation rules corresponding to accounts, environments, applications, teams, and cost centers, and decide how to apportion shared-service costs and handle missing tags.

Review budgets, anomaly detection, utilization, and cost per unit, and correlate changes in costs with deployments, traffic, data volume, and contract changes. Rather than unconditionally cutting monitoring or backups because costs have increased, compare alternatives that meet the quality objectives.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Cost Allocation and Visibility

checkpoints.prompt: We want to reduce the cost of an image-conversion job that can be rerun every night and only needs to finish by the deadline, even if it is interrupted. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Move all processing to Spot capacity unconditionally, without deciding how interruptions will be handled.
choices.explanation: The risks of missing results or exceeding the deadline cannot be assessed.

choices.text: Design interruption handling and retries, then consider interruptible capacity such as Spot capacity.
choices.explanation: This addresses both the purchasing model suited to the processing characteristics and the recovery conditions.

choices.text: Fix the maximum On-Demand capacity at all times without checking usage.
choices.explanation: This does not optimize capacity according to demand.

checkpoints.prompt: The cost of global content delivery is increasing. What should the architect investigate first?

choices.text: Measure the amount of data transferred among users, the edge, the origin, and Regions, along with the cache hit rate, latency, and failover routes.
choices.explanation: This enables comparison of the sources of the costs with the impact of changes on quality.

choices.text: Pin the deployment to the least expensive Region without checking the origin route during failures.
choices.explanation: This could fail to meet availability and latency requirements.

choices.text: Disable all caching without checking the data-transfer routes.
choices.explanation: This could increase costs and user latency.

checkpoints.prompt: Several teams share an analytics platform and want to optimize its costs based on the factors driving them. Which approach is the most appropriate?

choices.text: Look only at the total billed amount and stop backups for all teams.
choices.explanation: This evaluates neither the cost drivers nor the recovery requirements.

choices.text: Design an allocation scheme that identifies the account, environment, application, and owning team, and reconcile the budget, anomalies, and utilization with design changes.
choices.explanation: This allows costs to be traced back to the responsible owners and usage patterns for decision-making.
This loses both cost attribution and opportunities for improvement.
